Finding: Substantial seasonal rate divergence exists between summer peaks and winter troughs.
Evidence: August ADR commands a +$74.17/night premium over January (MLR p < 2.2e-16). Resort rates surge dramatically in summer.
Possible_Managerial_Action: Implement dynamic seasonal rate differentiation: lift minimum floor rates during June-Aug; package bundled F&B/spa deals in winter.
Limitation: Short 26-month dataset contains only one full prior summer; price sensitivity (elasticity) curves are unobserved.

Finding: Upgraded room categories (Suites F, G, H) command substantial, statistically significant premiums.
Evidence: Room G commands +$60.16/night and Room H +$63.84/night over baseline Room A (MLR p < 2.2e-16).
Possible_Managerial_Action: Protect suite inventory from premature discounted allocation; offer paid upgrades to standard room guests prior to arrival.
Limitation: Physical room capacity caps are unrecorded in PMS extract; upgrade willingness may vary across seasons.

Finding: Advance booking horizon (lead_time) strongly escalates cancellation probability.
Evidence: Each 30 days of lead time increases cancellation odds by +17.1% (OR_30 = 1.1706; OR = 1.0053/day). 100 days = +69.1% odds (distinguishing relative odds from probability).
Possible_Managerial_Action: Enforce progressive cancellation terms: require credit card pre-authorizations or tiered non-refundable discounts for lead times > 60 days.
Limitation: Causal effect unproven: long lead times may correlate with unobserved vacation uncertainty rather than causing cancellation.

Finding: Special requests and vehicle parking requirements signal high stay commitment in historical data.
Evidence: Each special request cuts cancellation odds by 59.0% (OR = 0.4099). Zero cancellations observed among parking requesters, though parking coefficient is statistically insignificant (p = 0.362, SE = 46.15) due to complete separation.
Possible_Managerial_Action: Engage high-lead-time guests with pre-arrival preference surveys (pillow choice, arrival time) to build rapport and confirm arrival intent.
Limitation: Parking predictor exhibits quasi-complete separation (p = 0.362) and cannot be artificially mandated; special requests reflect passive commitment rather than active intervention.

Finding: Simple Exponential Smoothing (SES) provides reliable 1-week-ahead rolling occupancy projections (~6.2% MAPE).
Evidence: SES achieved the lowest out-of-sample Test RMSE (93.7 Resort, 113.5 City). Dividing RMSE by 7 yields a rough scale conversion of ~13-16 rooms/day (not true daily uncertainty).
Possible_Managerial_Action: Proposed Heuristic Policy: Size permanent core housekeeping shifts to cover ~90% of expected weekly demand (or baseline minus 1 SD); utilize flexible agency staff for peaks, subject to local labor cost validation.
Limitation: Historical series (78 train weeks) is insufficient for classical 52-week seasonal decomposition. Weekly aggregation conceals intra-week day-of-week volatility.

Finding: High-risk wholesale groups exhibit severe cancellation rates despite non-refundable policies.
Evidence: Group segment cancellation rate is 61.2% (OR = 2.99). Non-refundable deposits have 99.4% cancellation rate in sample.
Possible_Managerial_Action: Tighten wholesale tour group release windows (attrition clauses) 45-60 days out to reclaim unsold blocks before retail demand peaks.
Limitation: Tour operator contract commission rates and penalty enforcement data are absent from the dataset.
